html:
The uprising of Asen and Peter was a revolt of Bulgarians and Vlachs in the lands between the Danube and the Balkan Mountains against Byzantine rule. It began on 26 October 1185 and led to the Second Bulgarian Empire.

The region had been part of the Byzantine Empire since Basil II conquered Bulgaria in 1018. In 1185 the new emperor Isaac II Angelos raised a special tax on herds to pay for his wedding. Two brothers, local lords, Theodore, who took the name Peter, and Asen, asked for land and were refused and insulted. They rose on the feast of Saint Demetrius, claiming the saint had left Thessalonica, just sacked by the Normans, to help them.

The rebels used the mountains well and allied with the Cumans of the steppe. Isaac's campaigns failed, and by about 1187 the empire had to accept a new Bulgarian state with its capital at Tarnovo. Both brothers were murdered by rivals in the 1190s, but their younger brother Kaloyan made the state a power in the Balkans.
